# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

## Plan review — 2026-11-05 (verified state)

Verified against the current checkout: main-street `dev` at `f4f083ed`, `core` submodule pinned at `5a16c2fb`, superproject working tree clean.

- **AC1 met** — `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains `achievementId: serial-seller` with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false` (13 entries in total).
- **AC3 met** — the `core` pointer now pins `5a16c2fb`, later than the `d2d1f322` recorded above, and that commit contains the manifest entry.
- **AC4 preconditions satisfied** — the parent mapping (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J) is now **committed**, not uncommitted as stated above: `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps all 13 challenges, and the manifest and the game-side mapping agree exactly (13 ↔ 13, no drift in either direction). `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` is the guard that exercises this.
- **AC2 unmet / external** — unchanged: blocked on `CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1` (Steamworks backend registration). Not verifiable from the repository.
- **AC5** — no documentation change beyond the manifest entry was identified as required; the existing 12-achievement pattern is followed.
- **AC6** — enforced by the dev-push gate; not re-run by this planning session.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-05 — Plan re-run (effort Extra Small / Low, so decomposition skipped): six review stages run, AC coverage 100% (proceed), stage set to `plan_complete`. Recorded the verified AC state above; no child work items created.

## Producer decision — AC2 waived (2026-11-10)

The producer reviewed this item and chose **option 1: waive AC2**.

**Rationale.** AC2 requires the `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` API name to be declared on the Steamworks partner backend. Both dependency items that carried that work in the `CG` store (Tableau-Card-Engine) — `CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ` (create the Steamworks project) and `CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1` (register the Main Street achievements) — were **deleted on 2026-11-01** with the comment *"Won't fix — Steam work cancelled by producer decision … superseded by the decision to drop the Steam distribution track."* There are no open `CG` items at all, and no Steamworks app exists, so there is no backend on which the API name could be declared. The criterion is therefore **waived**, not met: it becomes a prerequisite of any future decision to ship on Steam rather than a blocker on this item.

**Durable record.** The manifest (`core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`) remains the single source of truth for `achievementId ↔ steamApiName ↔ hidden`, and `core/docs/dev/steam-achievements-qa.md` still lists backend registration as a hard prerequisite for the real-account QA plan. If the Steam distribution track is ever revived, the first action is to create the Steamworks app and register all 13 API names — starting from the manifest, which is already correct.

**Verified AC state at the decision point** (`dev` @ `879231a1`, == `origin/dev`; `core` pinned at `a26d4bf0`):

- AC1 met — `serial-seller` → `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`, `hidden: false`, 13 entries.
- AC2 waived — see above.
- AC3 met — `git ls-tree HEAD core` = `a26d4bf0`, which contains the manifest entry.
- AC4 met — 13 challenge mappings ↔ 13 manifest ids, no drift either direction; `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` green.
- AC5 met — `README.md` §Challenges, `docs/dev/prd-milestone-2.md`, `core/docs/dev/steam-achievements-qa.md`.
- AC6 met — full suite green at the last dev-push gate (6752 passed, 3 skipped); no code change since.

This item was finalised as a **verification-only** completion: the deliverable (manifest entry, game mapping, drift guard) shipped in `dd11ea4` (core `d2d1f322`, since advanced to `a26d4bf0`), so the session produced no new commit.

## Impact

Every Main Street challenge — including the new Serial Seller — now has a matching persistent achievement defined in the shared launcher manifest and the game-side mapping, so a player's challenge completion has a Steam achievement to unlock and drift between the two sides fails a test instead of silently dropping the unlock.

# Staff ownership docs and full suite

## Goal

Update the player-facing rules documentation and the remaining code-comment references so they state that staff placement, relocation and applicant targeting are restricted to the acting seat's own businesses, then verify the full project suite is green.

## Parent acceptance criteria covered

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (`MainStreetEngineCommands`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner`, `MainStreetStateSerialize` JSDoc), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (hire/relocate rule now states placement is restricted to the acting seat's own businesses), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (shared staff rules sentence), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Scope

- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — the hire/relocate rule (the action table rows and the relocation note) states that placement and relocation are restricted to the acting seat's own businesses in competitive play.

data.description:
Add a true **Summary** tab to the end-of-turn Turn Summary overlay: the first tab, selected by default, showing only the closed turn's headline information — what each player/AI did, what happened (events), and how income/reputation/score moved — with each figure carrying a tooltip that breaks it down the way today's per-player tab does.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary overlay opens on one player's full profit/loss statement, so the first thing a player sees is a dense per-account breakdown rather than what actually happened in the turn. There is no single view that answers "who did what, what happened, and did everyone gain or lose?" — the player must tab through every seat and read four sections per seat to assemble that picture.

## Users

- **Single-player player** — wants a one-glance recap of the day ("I placed a business, an incident hit, I earned +18 and my score is 42") without reading a full P&L.
- **Competitive player** — wants to see, in one place, what each rival did this shared day and how each seat's income, reputation and score moved, before drilling into any one seat's statement.
- **AI seats (as presented subjects)** — their actions, events and deltas must appear in the same summary so a competitive turn reads as a shared day, not just the human's day.

Example user stories:

- As a single-player player, I open the Turn Summary and immediately see my major actions, the incident that hit, and my income/reputation/score change with my resulting balances.
- As a competitive player, I open the Turn Summary and see every seat's major actions for the shared day plus each seat's income/reputation/score change and balance, then hover any figure to see that seat's breakdown.
- As a player who wants detail, I switch from `[ Summary ]` to `[ You ]` / `[ AI 1 ]` and get exactly today's full profit/loss statement for that seat.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Turn Summary overlay presents a `[ Summary ]` tab as its **first** tab and selects it by default, in both single-player and competitive closings, leaving the existing per-player tabs (`You` / `AI n`) unchanged and still selectable.
- The Summary tab's sections render in the confirmed order **Major actions → Events → Income/Reputation/Score** (producer answer Q1 = A).
- The Summary tab lists the closed turn's **major actions** — player- and AI-initiated actions only (placing a business, hiring staff, playing an upgrade/event, moving a card to hand, selling, laying off, closing a street card, loans, challenge completions) — per seat, attributed with the seat label (`You` / `AI n`) used elsewhere in the UI. Turn headers and the turn's own monetary summary rows (income/reputation lines) are excluded, because the sections below already present those figures (producer answer Q2). The list is derived from the game's own record of what happened that turn, not from UI-invented figures.
- Action classification is structural, not textual: the turn record exposes an explicit action marker (an optional category on `LogEntry`, set wherever a player- or AI-initiated action is logged), so no rendered action row depends on matching log message text.
- The Summary tab shows the day's **income change and resulting balance**, **reputation change and resulting balance** and **score change and resulting balance**, one row per metric with every player/AI seat's change and closing balance listed on that row (producer answer Q3 = A), formatted with the panel's existing signed convention (`+N` / `-N` / `0`).
- The Summary tab shows the turn's **events** (the resolved incident and the effect it applied) as their own labelled section, rendered **before** the income/reputation/score figures (producer answer Q1 = A).
- Every seat's figure on the Summary tab carries a hover/tap tooltip giving that seat's **breakdown** equivalent to today's per-player tab (per-business income phases, per-card expense categories, incident/one-off reconciliation, net reconciliation), and the tooltip figures reconcile to the headline figure they annotate.
- The Summary tab participates in tab navigation: pointer selection, Left/Right keyboard cycling and the selected-tab preservation after a mid-game loan take all include it, and selection is signalled with the panel's existing bold-selected convention.
- Presentation-only and absent-safe: no state mutation, no RNG consumption, no new persisted field; a result carrying no ledger of either shape still advances the closing immediately instead of stranding it; reduced-motion, replay and headless pacing are unchanged.
- Unit tests cover a pure Summary-tab model builder: the confirmed section order, per-seat action attribution (player and AI), exclusion of turn headers and monetary summary rows from the actions section, one-row-per-metric layout with a change and a balance per seat, signed formatting, absent-safe degradation when the turn record omits actions/events, and reconciliation of headline figures with the existing P&L projection.
- Browser (Phaser/jsdom) tests cover the Summary tab being first and default-selected in both modes, its rendered sections, its tooltips on hover/tap, tab switching away and back, and the selected Summary tab surviving a post-loan-take re-render.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably the Turn Summary sections of `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players now open the Turn Summary on a single headline view of the day — who did what, what happened, and how everyone's income, reputation and score moved — instead of a dense per-player account, while the full breakdown stays one hover (or one tab) away.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only: the summary is projected from already-committed turn data; no accounting is recomputed by the UI and no new authoritative figure is introduced.
- Reuse, don't fork: the existing P&L projection (`PLProjection`) and the existing tooltip content builders (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`) stay the single source of breakdown truth so the Summary and per-player tabs can never drift.
- Overlay pattern compliance (`AGENTS.md` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201, dismissal via `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX through `safePlaySound`.
- Panel geometry is fixed (`PANEL_WIDTH` 680 × `PANEL_HEIGHT` 640): the summary layout must stay within it for a full competitive roster (the section must reflow or bound its row count rather than overflow).
- All new user-facing strings go through the core-engine `t()` i18n path, matching the existing ledger tooltip keys; UK English spelling.
- Action classification is structural, not textual: add an optional action marker to `LogEntry` and set it at every player- or AI-initiated action `addLog` call site; no rendered action row may depend on matching log message text.

## Existing state

- The overlay is one unified tabbed P&L panel: `presentTurnSummaryPanel()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`, entered from `showTurnSummaryDialog()` (single-player) and `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog()` (competitive). Tabs are built by `buildPLTabsFromTurnSummary()` / `buildPLTabsFromCompetitiveSummary()`, each tab body rendered from a `PLProjection`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` is the Phaser-free model: `buildTurnSummary()` (single-player headline figures), `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary()` (per-seat rows), `buildPLProjection()` / `buildPLFromTurnSummary()` / `buildPLFromCompetitiveRow()` (the statement), `buildPLTabs*()` (the tab strip).
- Per-row breakdowns already exist: `PLLineBreakdown` carries per-business income items and per-card expense items, and `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` builds the tooltip content (`buildIncomeLineTooltip`, `buildExpenseLineTooltip`, `buildIncidentLineTooltip`, `buildOneOffLineTooltip`, `buildNetLineTooltip`, `buildTotalLineTooltip`, `buildContextLineTooltip`).
- The turn's narrative record already exists: `state.activityLog` (`LogEntry[]`, each with `turn`, `text`, `type`, and optional `seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`), written solely through `appendActivityLogEntry()` in `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts`, with `addLog()` (seat-attributed) and `addLogShared()` (turn-level) as the two producers. It carries player-initiated actions (place business, hire staff, play upgrade/event, move to hand, sell, lay off, close, loans, challenge completions) **mixed with** monetary summary rows (per-turn income/reputation lines) and turn headers.
- The resolved incident is on the result (`TurnResult.incident`, an `EventCard | null`, plus `incidentCoinChange` / `incidentRepChange`); the competitive ledger does not name the incident, so competitive summary rows carry `incidentName: null` today.
- Existing tests to extend: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-pl-model.test.ts`, `turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`, `turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts`, `turn-summary-pl-overlay.browser.test.ts`, `turn-summary-tooltip.browser.test.ts`, `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Model** — a pure builder (in `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) producing a Summary-tab model in the confirmed order: per-seat major actions (player- and AI-initiated only), the turn's events, then one row per metric (Income / Reputation / Score) carrying every seat's change and closing balance, each figure paired with the `PLProjection`-derived tooltip payload it annotates. Absent-safe: a turn record missing actions or events yields empty sections, never a thrown error.
2. **Overlay** — a `[ Summary ]` tab inserted before the per-player tabs and marked default; its body renders the model's sections with per-figure tooltip zones (`attachHudTooltipZone`), inside the existing panel geometry.
3. **Tooltips** — extend `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` with the content builders the Summary tab needs, reusing the existing per-line builders so a summary tooltip's breakdown matches that seat's per-player tab.
4. **Action classification** — source the major-action rows from `state.activityLog` for the closed turn, selected by a new optional action marker on `LogEntry` that every player- and AI-initiated action `addLog` call site sets; turn headers and the per-turn monetary summary rows carry no marker, so they never appear in the actions section (producer answer Q2).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — new pure Summary-tab model builder alongside `buildTurnSummary()` / `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary()`; reuse `PLProjection` for tooltip payloads.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — insert the `[ Summary ]` tab, mark it default, render its body and attach its tooltips within the fixed panel geometry.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — Summary-row tooltip content builders and their i18n keys (reusing the existing per-line builders).
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — optional structural action marker on `LogEntry` (producer answer Q2).
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` and the `addLog` call sites for player-/AI-initiated actions — set the marker (turn headers and monetary summary rows deliberately leave it unset).
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-summary-tab*.test.ts` — new unit/browser suites; extend `turn-summary-pl-overlay.browser.test.ts` for tab-strip parity.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Turn Summary dialog and competitive panel sections document the new default tab.

## Related work

- **MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY** — Turn summary should be laid out as an account profit/loss statement (completed): parent of the tabbed P&L overlay this tab extends; its producer answers (Q1=A, Q2=A, Q3=A) fix the statement shape and the human-default tab this item now supersedes as the default view.
- **MS-0MW5ER6HC000HVQ8** — Implement tabbed P&L overlay (completed): the tab strip, rendering and keyboard navigation being extended here.
- **MS-0MW5EQ0BA004E4QY** / **MS-0MW5EPEXW000AZKO** — P&L projection model and its unit tests: the breakdown source the Summary tab's tooltips reuse.
- **MS-0MW7QQ5QU007XXC0** / **MS-0MW7QQ65P006N3KA** / **MS-0MW7QQ286007L4J3** — ledger row tooltips, competitive per-seat tooltip parity and their browser verification: the tooltip attachment contract the Summary tab must follow.
- **MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO** / **MS-0MW6GPRL6001DFCF** — end-of-turn ledger tooltips and the pointer-blocker fix: existing panel interaction behaviour that must not regress.
- **MS-0MW5ERPLV004WZHR** — Update Turn Summary documentation (completed): the docs section to extend.
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** — Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (completed): the single-presentation-path constraint.
- **MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK** / **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** — competitive per-seat summary rows and the competitive end-of-turn summary dialog epic: competitive parity for the new tab.
- Related docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate; Competitive Turn Summary panel), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/dev/testing.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Section order (confirmed).** Producer answer Q1 = A: Major actions → Events → Income/Reputation/Score. The seed's numbering is superseded by its own "events (before income/reputation/score)" note; browser assertions pin this order.
- **"Major action" scope (confirmed).** Producer answer Q2: player- and AI-initiated actions only — turn headers and the per-turn monetary summary rows are excluded so the section never repeats the figures shown below it.
- **Classification integrity (medium).** The activity log mixes action rows with monetary summary rows, so the new `LogEntry` action marker is the only discriminator. Mitigation: a guard test that every action-producing call site sets the marker, plus an absent-safe model path that renders an empty actions section rather than guessing.
- **Panel overflow (medium).** A summary tab with a full competitive roster (actions + events + 3×N figures) can exceed the fixed 680×640 panel. Mitigation: bounded row counts with an "…and N more" affordance, compact typography, and a browser test at maximum supported roster size.
- **Drift between Summary and per-player tabs (medium).** Two renderings of the same figures can diverge. Mitigation: both project from the same `PLProjection` / model values; unit tests assert reconciliation.
- **Existing tooltip/pointer behaviour regressions (low-medium).** Tooltip attachment, tap-toggle and the `[ Next Turn ]` pointer blocker are pinned by earlier items. Mitigation: extend the existing browser suites rather than writing parallel ones.
- **Scope creep.** Live activity-log feed behaviour, incident-balance rules, the loan selector and the competitive closing animation are out of scope; any new opportunity found during implementation becomes a linked work item, not added scope.
- **Assumption.** The Summary tab appears in both single-player and competitive closings (the panel is one shared renderer); single-player shows a single `You` row set with a non-interactive tab strip as today.
- **Assumption.** "Events" means the resolved incident and the effect it applied (the panel already carries `TurnResult.incident` plus its coin/reputation deltas); played event cards surface through the actions section as player-initiated actions rather than a second events list. If the producer wants drawn/played event cards in the Events section too, that is an additive change to the same section.
- **Assumption.** The Income/Reputation/Score rows show the human seat plus every non-eliminated AI seat in competitive play, and the single `You` seat in single-player — the same seat set the tab strip already shows.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Section order — does "events (before income/reputation/score)" mean the Events section renders **above** the income/reputation/score figures, or that events merely resolve before them in the turn sequence (keeping the seed's numbered order: actions → figures → events)? — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — Actions → Events → Income/Reputation/Score.** Recorded in the ACs and pinned by the browser assertions. Source: producer reply on this work item.
- Q: "Major actions" scope — which activity-log rows belong in the Summary tab? (a) player-initiated actions only, excluding the per-turn income/reputation summary rows the tab already presents; (b) every activity-log row for the turn; (c) every row including turn headers. — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **player- and AI-initiated actions** — i.e. option (a), actions only, covering every seat. Turn headers and monetary summary rows stay out. Implemented structurally via the new `LogEntry` action marker. Source: producer reply on this work item.
- Q: Income/reputation/score layout on the Summary tab — (a) one row per metric listing each seat's change and balance (each seat segment its own tooltip); (b) one block per player with three metric rows; (c) a full grid of player × metric rows. — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — one row per metric**, with every seat's change and resulting balance on that row and a per-seat tooltip. Source: producer reply on this work item.
- Q: Should the Summary tab be the default view in competitive closings as well as single-player? — Answer (agent, researched): **Yes** — single-player and competitive closings share one renderer (`presentTurnSummaryPanel`), and the seed asks for a summary of "players/AI", so the tab is first and default in both modes. Research: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` → *Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate*.
data.title: Turn summary shows a true summary tab
